title: Arithmetic fundamental group after a finite constant-field extension
statement: Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with fixed algebraic closure $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], let $m\geq1$, and let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme in the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $X_0^{(m)}=X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m}$ using the base-change construction [def-pc-base-change], regarded as an $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-scheme. Then $X_0^{(m)}$ is connected. Choose a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ and give $X_0^{(m)}$ and $X_0$ the geometric points obtained by composing with $X\to X_0^{(m)}\to X_0$. The continuous homomorphism $\pi_1(X_0^{(m)},\bar x)\to\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)$ induced by the projection $X_0^{(m)}\to X_0$ [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] is injective and identifies the arithmetic étale fundamental group $\pi_1(X_0^{(m)})$ of [def-wf-fundamental-representation] with the inverse image of $\operatorname{Gal}(k/\mathbf F_{q^m})$ under the canonical projection $\pi_1(X_0)\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$. Under this identification, the kernel of the projection to $\operatorname{Gal}(k/\mathbf F_{q^m})$ is the same geometric fundamental group $\pi_1(X)$ as for $X_0$.
